content:
8 ◆ The Āgama Encyclopaedia
corpus seeks to promote the other three values of life also
(viz. tri-varga: dharma, artha and kāma); hence the superior
merit of the "ekāyana", which teaches the worship of god
who has descended on earth and among mankind, for the
sake of realizing final emancipation:
आद्यमेकायनं वेदं मोक्षैकफलक्षणम्।
प्रकाशयध्वं सर्वेषां सद्धर्माश्च विशेषतः ॥
तत्र तत्रावतीर्णं मां स्वयंव्यक्तादिभेदतः ।
संपूजयध्वं सर्वेषां मोक्षलाभाय भूतले ॥
This position also brings out the difference between
the ekāyana and the Veda. The Vedas are meant only for
the persons who are eligible to their study and who are
qualified to perform the rituals prescribed therein, while
the ekāyana is meant for all alike (sarveṣām), for all are
eligible to realize final emancipation. Indeed, it was
claimed by the Pāñcarātra authorities that this ekāyana is
the original veda (mūla-veda), the veda (the word of God)
that existed before the divisions of Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman
came about. Utpala's Spanda-Kārikā cites this view:
ऋगादिभेदेन वेदशाखाविभजनात् प्राक् ।
विद्यमाना एकायनाशाखैव मूलवेद इति ॥
The Pāñcarātra texts proceed to describe the extant
Vedas as only large branches of the huge ekāyana tree,
for the ekāyana was propounded by Vāsudeva himself
who is the source of the world: it is in fact the original
Veda.
महतो वेदवृक्षस्य मूलभूतो महानयम् ।
ऋगाद्याः स्कन्धभूतास्ते शाखाभूताश्च योगिनः ॥
summary: This page from 'The Āgama Encyclopaedia' discusses the concept of "ekāyana," presenting it as a tradition superior to the Vedas for achieving final emancipation (mokṣa). It argues that while the Vedas are restricted to a select group of qualified individuals, ekāyana is universally accessible to all (sarveṣām). The text, citing Pāñcarātra authorities and Utpala's Spanda-Kārikā, claims that ekāyana is the original, primordial Veda (mūla-veda) that existed before the later divisions into Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman. The extant Vedas are described metaphorically as branches of the great "ekāyana tree," which was propounded by Vāsudeva.
author_motivation: The provided text is an encyclopaedia entry, not a preface, so it does not directly state the author's personal motivation for writing the book. However, it describes the motivation of the religious corpus being discussed, stating that it "seeks to promote the other three values of life also (viz. tri-varga: dharma, artha and kāma)" while ultimately teaching the worship of God "for the sake of realizing final emancipation."
book_genesis: The provided text does not contain information about how 'The Āgama Encyclopaedia' was created. Instead, it describes a theological genesis of the Vedas, positing that they originated as branches from the singular, original "ekāyana tree" or "mūla-veda" which was propounded by Vāsudeva.
intended_audience: The scholarly tone, use of specialized Sanskrit terminology (e.g., ekāyana, tri-varga, sarveṣām), inclusion of Devanagari script, and citation of specific philosophical texts (Pāñcarātra, Spanda-Kārikā) suggest that the intended audience consists of academics, researchers, and students in the fields of Indology, Hindu philosophy, religious studies, and Sanskrit.
